chapter: Return to New York, addiction, health and the NBC job
title: The late 1950s: cabaret card, the 1957 arrest and heavy heroin use
summary: He did not play in the late 1950s; a probation technicality followed his arrest and he began mainlining.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Well, I was gigging with him intermittently, you know.
Yeah. Because whenever he had a regular group, Red Mitchell was with him, because they were sort of related in marriage or something, you know, so he used him mostly.
In the late '50s you weren't playing. Is that right?
In the late '50s, no. Because they snatched my cabaret card.
And then in the early '60s you were in California most of the time.
I was out here in the '50s, from '53 up until the last part of '55, December of '55. Yeah, '55. And then I was going to New York, you know, because my probation
was almost up and the Probation Officer told me I didn't have to come back anymore. And I wasn't aware that I had to go before a judge to have it finalized.
And I got arrested in New York in '57.
That was when you did time.

Yeah. And then they brought up this probation violation. I said, 'What is that?' And the man told me I didn't have to come back. So these -- the probation officer over there says, 'Well, it's just a technicality. We knew where you were, you know, and everything, but you were supposed to see the Judge before you left.' I said, 'Well, no-one told me anything about it.' He says, 'Well, all you'll have to do is two weeks. And you've been in here that long, so forget it.' You know. So the '60s didn't hold too much for me here. Like I continued to use heroin, real heavy then. That's when I started mainlining.

No. Let's see. It was in the '60s, yes. But like the idle mind makes Jack a dull boy, you know, and it's the devil's workshop. I couldn't get any jobs or anything. I was just hanging out with the fellows, you know.
